summary: Pinned model unexpectedly demoted during edge rate-shedding, causing intermittent canary responses
description:
Issue summary: Customer (Novum HealthTech) observed that several user sessions that were pinned to their dedicated model version gpt-large-v1 started receiving responses from the canary variant intermittently during a peak traffic window. Impact: ~8% of requests from pinned sessions returned canary outputs between 2026-03-10T14:02 and 2026-03-10T14:45 UTC, causing subtle semantic differences in model output for live users. Pinned sessions should not be demoted under normal operation.

Environment: prod-us-east (dedicated capacity pool: novum-pool-3).

Steps to reproduce:
1) Create a session with version pin header X-Model-Pin: gpt-large-v1 for a tenant on novum-pool-3.
2) Simulate sustained burst of requests from many tenants to trigger edge rate-shedding (we used a controlled load test matching observed QPS).
3) Observe routing decisions in trace and request logs (trace IDs included below) where session affinity token is present but route resolves to canary variant.

Expected behavior: Requests with an active pin should route to the pinned model variant until pin expires or is explicitly changed.
Observed behavior: During the rate-shedding window our edge layer deprioritized pinned routes and allowed canary routes to be selected to satisfy SLOs; pinned sessions saw intermittent responses from canary variant.

Relevant logs/traces (sample):
- trace: us-east:trace-20260310-14:12:35: t=trace-8af3cf (session token: s-9c2b). Route decision: edge-proxy rate-shed priority=low -> routing-layer selected fallback route canary/gpt-large-v1-canary.
- request id: req-4f7a2f9b: pin header present, backend assigned: canary node id cn-42.

Notes: Customer reported via support channel #support-novum and provided 6 sample request IDs. We reproduced locally using controlled traffic and confirmed similar route inversion under the same rate-shedding config.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Pin session to gpt-large-v1 via X-Model-Pin header.
2) Generate a synthetic QPS spike across multiple tenants to trigger edge rate shedding policies.
3) Observe routing decisions in trace logs for pinned sessions.
4) Verify that the backend returned canary variant responses intermittently.
logs: Selected sample traces: trace-8af3cf (see description), trace-8af3d1, trace-8af3e2. Edge proxy logs show 'rate-shed: true' with policy id rs-edge-priority-2. Routing-layer debug shows 'pin-resolve: ok' then 'deprioritize-pin: true' decision event. Serving runtime logs show request handed to canary pool node cn-42 with model tag gpt-large-v1-canary.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-10 14:20 UTC - Initial reproducible case validated by SRE: controlled load caused edge rate-shed to activate and routing decisions to deprioritize pinned flows.
Hypothesis A: Edge rate-shedding policy incorrectly treats pinned routes as low-priority under global contention due to missing pin-priority override in policy evaluation.

Hypothesis B: A short-circuit in routing-layer evaluation reorders candidate list after pin check when edge-proxy attaches a 'shed' tag, leading to selection of canary nodes with higher free capacity.
Checked config: edge rate-shedding rules (rs-edge-priority-*) did not include explicit 'pin:true' clause prior to 2026-03-10; default behavior was to evaluate available capacity only.
SRE ran a test toggling pin-priority flag in staging which preserved pinned routing under simulated edge load; suggests config deficiency rather than runtime bug.
Related PR 6b9f4d3 updated routing-layer to accept 'shed' tags and reorder candidate list for best-effort SLO compliance; change did not include safeguard for pinned sessions.
Cross-referenced SUP-31147 for earlier pinning anomalies during rollouts; different trigger but similar symptom of pin overshadowing.
We collected additional telemetry: ~92% of pinned requests stayed pinned, ~8% diverted during peak short window; average diversion duration per session was 1-3 minutes.
Engineering determined root cause: policy config omission — rate-shedding prioritized global SLOs without honoring explicit pin flags.
comments: Customer (Novum) initial: 'We started seeing odd responses in prod around 14:05 UTC. Several ongoing user flows returned an older canary output. This is breaking a small fraction of user workflows.'
Support (Maya): 'Thanks — we're investigating. Can you share request IDs and whether pin header was present?' (attached 6 IDs).
SRE (Ethan): 'Reproduced with controlled load. Edge policy rs-edge-priority-2 active. Pin header checked but deprioritized by shed tag. Engaging routing team.'

Routing eng (Sofia Nguyen): 'Found that recent reorder logic added to favor low-latency nodes when 'shed' tag is present. That logic didn't exempt pinned sessions; proposing a config hotfix to treat pinned:true as highest priority.'
Customer acceptance: 'Workaround acceptable if we get a mitigation and root cause. Please advise ETA.'
Support update (Maya): 'We have a hotfix planned to land within the hour to add a pin-exempt clause to the edge evaluation. We'll follow up once change is deployed and confirm telemetry.'
SRE follow-up: 'Hotfix deployed 2026-03-10T15:05 UTC. Post-deploy checks show diversion rate dropped to 0.2% in subsequent 60 minutes; customer confirmed no further user complaints.'
resolution: Root cause: Edge rate-shedding policy omitted an explicit 'pin' exemption; combined with routing-layer reordering for shed-tagged nodes, pinned sessions could be demoted. Mitigation: 1) Hotfix (config change) applied to edge policy to set 'pin:exempt' in evaluation clause (deployed 2026-03-10T15:05 UTC). 2) Routing-layer patch (PR#1587) added defensive check to prevent candidate reordering for sessions with active pin tokens. Post-deploy verification: diversion <0.5% and customer confirmed. Follow-ups: schedule a test matrix to cover rate-shedding + pin combinations, add automated regression test to CI for pin-exempt behavior, and update runbook.
resolution_notes: Hotfix deployed to prod-us-east at 2026-03-10T15:05 UTC (edge config rs-edge-priority-2 updated).
Routing-layer change merged PR#1587 and rolled out in canary + prod on 2026-03-11.
Customer notification sent 2026-03-12 with incident summary and follow-up plan.
follow_up_actions: Add CI test that simulates edge rate-shedding while sessions have active pins (owner: routing-team).
Update Runbook: include step to verify pin-exempt flag when modifying rate-shedding rules (owner: SRE).
Audit other rate-shedding policies across regions to ensure pin exemptions exist (owner: platform-ops).
Schedule post-incident review and include findings in the fortnightly reliability forum (owner: Eng Manager).
